newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - October 1.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail:
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
FORMER PREMIER GETS APEX COURT'S REPRIVE IN CHEATING CASE

The Supreme Court exempted former premier Narasimha Rao from appearing in person as accused in the Lakhubhai Pathak cheating case. The court's decision was prompted by hightened threat perceptions from Sikh and Kashmiri militants to Rao's life. Rao got further respite as the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) special Judge adjourned hearing in the cheating case to October 9. On that day the former Prime Minister is supposed to appear before the CBI special Judge as a co-acused in the case.
The Times Of India
GOVERNMENT COUNSEL IN CHEATING CASE QUITS

Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) counsel Gopal Subramaniam handling the $100,000 Lakhubhai Pathak case has resigned from the special prosecutorship in protest. It is said he was asked by the United Front Government to bail out former Premier Narasimha Rao in the cheating case. CBI director Joginder Singh had reportedly asked not to oppose Rao's bail plea in the case. His letter to the CBI counsel referred to the Law Minister's directive saying that the Attorney General had consented that Rao's plea for bail should not be objected.
Financial Express
$1 BLN CAP ON FII INFLOW MOOTED

The Finance Ministry may impose an annual cap of $1 billion on investments by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in the domestic debt market. Plans are also on board to put a ceiling of $100 million for individual FII debt schemes. The FII debt flows would thus now come under the overall external commercial borrowing (ECB) limit. The existing ECB ceiling stands at $6.5 billion. This would be calibrated to consider FII inflows through the debt route. The Finance Ministry's new ruling is part of its guidelines to oversee FII debt in flows.
CENTRAL BANK SOUNDS NOTE OF CAUTION FOR WEAKER BANKS

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) plans to put a ring around the weaker state-run banks. The central bank wants these banks to consolidate their positions instead of focussing on growth. RBI's move is prompted by reasoning that weaker banks may take on a higher proportion of non-performing assets on their books as a result of their incremental advances. The outgoing RBI Deputy Governor informed that weaker banks should focus on recovery and not on new clients.
FINANCE MINISTER FOR ENHANCING FUND QUOTAS

The Finance Minister said India would continue its economic reforms. The Minister also called for global support for the Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on a self-financing basis. Addressing an IMF meeting in Washington, the minister stressed on the need for further reduction in trade restrictions imposed by industrialised countries. He called for resisting protectionist tendencies emerging in industrialised countries out of fear about competition from developing countries.
The Economic Times
ENRON-BECHTEL MARRIAGE ON THE ROCKS

Bechtel Enterprises Inc may quit as the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractor in Dabhol Power Project (DPC), of Enron Development Corp, in Maharashtra. Enron's Dabhol Power Company (DPC) was facing a few hitches in retaining Bechtel as partner in the power project on account of delay due to political and legal problems. Bechtel has bid for a few other power projects in India, including hydel projects in the North-East. In case Bechtel withdrew from the project, DPC plans to go in for international competitive bidding for selecting its new EPC contractor.
BHEL POSTS 50 PCT HIKE IN CONTRACT ORDER

Bharat Heavy Electrical Ltd (BHEL) has achieved the highest order book position in recent years by finalising contracts valued at over 100 billion rupees. The main contracts awarded to BHEL in the past six months are for the Bakreshwar unit in West Bengal, Kayam Kulam project in Kerala, and the Raichur power plant in Karnataka. The company registered an increase in the turnover by 18 percent (48.3 billion rupees) and a hike of 60 percent (58.2 billion rupees) in the profit before tax.
The Observer
CENTRAL BANK MAY STEP IN TO EASE CREDIT SITUATION

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has drawn plans to boost the sagging pace of exports. RBI plans to extend the period for export refinance beyond the 90 days limit. Sources said, the central bank planned to announce a proposal to this effect as part of its busy season credit policy. Export growth during the first four months of the current financial year (April-July) stood at only 11 percent, against 28 percent in the same period in the previous fiscal. The Finance Ministry and RBI were under pressure from the exporters to raise export credit, particularly the refinance facility.
MODI TIE-UP WITH DISTACOM, MOTOROLA OKAYED

The Union Cabinet has okayed the change of partners in Modi Telecom. The company has been allowed to replace its original foreign partners Vanguard and Thailand's Telecom International Corp with Distacom Communications and Motorola. Modi Telecom was set up to provide cellular telecom services. The Cabinet Committee on Foreign Investment has allowed Distacom to hold 39 percent and Motorola 10 percent equity in Modi Telecom. Modi Telecom holds the licence for cellular phone services in Karnataka and Punjab.
Business Line
SICK STEEL FIRM ATTRACTS ONLY TWO BIDS

The Steel Ministry has received only two bids for reviving the ailing Indian Iron and Steel Company (IISCO). The bidders are Mitsui of Japan and TPE of Russia. The Ministry had set September 30 as the deadline for receiving bids for forming a joint venture with Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL) to revive IISCO. This decision was taken following refusal by Union Government to fund IISCO's revival plans. IISCO is a 100 percent subsidiary of SAIL. SAIL would hold 51 percent equity in the joint venture.
BOMBAY BOURSE INDICES TO BE RECAST

The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) has decided to reconstitute BSE 100 National Index, BSE 200 and Dollex. BSE has replaced 15 scrips in the revised BSE 100 index and 10 scrips in BSE 200. The change in calculation of these indices will be reflected from October 14, a BSE release said. With the change in the composition of these indices, BSE 100 index may now have a market capitalisation of 2354.5 billion rupees. And BSE 200 index a market capitalisation of 2823.3 billion rupees.
